items.title: Clueso MCP
items.name: Clueso MCP
items.summary: Create and edit videos by chatting
items.description: Make videos with Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI agent. Give Clueso an idea, deck, reference video, or recording, and it handles the whole video production: storyboard, scenes, voiceover, music, and editing, on-brand. Everything stays editable, by hand or by chat.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt Community! 👋

I’m Neel, co-founder of Clueso.

We launched Clueso here last year with a pretty simple idea: turn rough screen recordings into polished product videos in minutes.

The response was incredible. Thousands of people started using Clueso, and this community made us #1 Product of the Day, Week, and Month.

Over the last year, we kept seeing people push Clueso beyond what we originally built it for. They wanted to start with more than a screen recording. They wanted to make more kinds of videos. And increasingly, they wanted AI to do more of the actual work.

So today we’re launching Clueso MCP.

Now you can create and edit videos directly from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent.

Give it a prompt and whatever material you have: a screen recording, deck, document, URL, Figma file, raw footage, reference video you like, or just an idea.

Clueso takes it from there. It plans the video, creates the scenes, writes the script, generates the AI voiceover, adds music, motion graphics, captions and animations, edits everything together, and applies your branding.

In fact, our product hunt launch video above was made entirely with Clueso MCP.

Basically, you tell it what you want to make, and it makes the video with you.

The part we care a lot about is control.

A lot of AI video tools feel like black boxes: you prompt them, get a finished clip back, and if something isn’t quite right, your main option is to keep regenerating.

Clueso is different because there’s a powerful video editor underneath the agent. Everything it creates remains editable. You can open the project and change anything yourself, or just keep chatting with the agent.

You could be a marketer making a launch video, a founder making a product demo, a freelancer creating something for a client, a small business making marketing content, or just someone with an idea they want to turn into a great video.

Here’s what you can do with it:

  • Create from inspiration. Give Clueso a few videos you like or a moodboard. It understands the look, feel, and creative direction you’re going for, then creates a full video around your own content, product, and brand.

  • Create pretty much any kind of video. Launch and marketing videos, product demos, walkthroughs, tutorials, explainers, social content, complex motion graphics, animated sequences, logo animations and more.

  • Edit however you want. Jump into the Clueso editor and make changes yourself, or just chat with the agent and ask it to make the edits for you.

  • Build custom workflows around video. Because Clueso works through MCP, you can connect it with tools like Figma, Slack, Linear, social platforms, your CRM, support tools and more and make video creation, editing and distribution part of a larger automated workflow.

So a feature can ship and turn into a launch video, a finished design can become an explainer, or a completed video can automatically move into the next step of your workflow.

Making a video no longer has to start with opening a video editor. You can tell your agent what you need, let it do the work, and still have complete control whenever you want to jump in yourself.

items.title: Makersclaw 2.0
items.name: Makersclaw 2.0
items.summary: The operating system for a company run by agents
items.description: MakersClaw 2.0 turns a goal into the apps, agents and automations needed to get it done. We originally launched MakersClaw as AI employees that lived in Slack, Teams and Telegram. We rebuilt it around a different idea: instead of hiring an agent for a role, tell MakersClaw what you want done. It builds the tools for the job, runs them continuously, remembers the work and operates within a budget you set. Today it starts with go-to-market
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt 👋 Shreyans here, maker of MakersClaw.

We first launched MakersClaw here in June as AI employees you could hire into Slack, Teams and Telegram.

Today we're relaunching as part of Astra Day, after rebuilding the product around a different idea.


MakersClaw is no longer primarily a chatbot you give a role to. You give it a goal.


MakersClaw figures out what needs to exist to pursue that goal — an app, an agent, automations, or some combination of them — builds those things into your workspace, connects them to your tools and runs the work.


Sometimes that means a research agent. Sometimes it needs a lead inbox, CRM, approval queue or recurring workflow. Instead of forcing every job through chat, MakersClaw can build the interface appropriate for the work.


Why we rebuilt it

AI made building software dramatically cheaper. A founder can ship a product in a weekend. But selling it is still weekly, repetitive, tool-heavy work.


We thought agents should be able to do much more of that work.


The problem with the agents we were using was that they were still session-based. They'd complete a task, lose context, ask to be restarted and wait for another prompt.


MakersClaw 2.0 is built around work that continues.


Tell it something like:


"Help me find and reach our first 50 customers."


You can watch the first run, inspect what it built, approve the important decisions and set a budget. After that, it can keep running and come back when it needs you.


Company files, decisions and results live in shared workspace memory, so agents can pick up where previous work left off rather than starting from scratch.


Today we're starting with go-to-market: research, content, outbound, follow-ups and the surrounding workflows. The App Store is still small and there are integrations we haven't tested deeply yet.


That's part of why we're launching now.


Try giving MakersClaw one real growth job you need done this week. If it gets stuck, builds the wrong thing or asks you to do something it should have handled itself, tell me here.


I'll be around all day.

Guys, what an intense day, isn't it?

How mny new users did you manage to bring to your product today, and how much feedback did you get?

The idea of giving an agent a goal instead of just a task is really interesting. The part about it continuously running and building the workflows it needs around that goal is especially compelling.

Curious to see how this evolves as more real-world workflows get added. 🚀

items.description: Lumiko records your screen and edits the footage while you work. It tracks your cursor and clicks, then builds smooth zoom and pan moves over them automatically, no keyframes. top_comments: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I built Lumiko because I kept losing an hour to keyframes after every five-minute recording. The zoom-and-pan you see in slick tutorial videos usually comes from someone manually placing markers over every click, and I got tired of it. Lumiko watches where your cursor goes while you record, then generates that zoom and pan movement on its own once you stop. You still get a full timeline editor for trimming and reordering clips, plus Smart Blur for hiding sensitive info like API keys before you share anything. Everything renders on your machine. No account, no upload step, no waiting on a server queue. Pro is $9, one time, no subscription. It removes the watermark, unlocks 4K exports, and covers 3 devices for life. Would love to hear what part of your current recording workflow eats the most time. That's what I'm building toward next.

items.title: Makersclaw 2.0
items.name: Makersclaw 2.0
items.summary: The operating system for a company run by agents
items.description: MakersClaw 2.0 turns a goal into the apps, agents and automations needed to get it done. We originally launched MakersClaw as AI employees that lived in Slack, Teams and Telegram. We rebuilt it around a different idea: instead of hiring an agent for a role, tell MakersClaw what you want done. It builds the tools for the job, runs them continuously, remembers the work and operates within a budget you set. Today it starts with go-to-market
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt 👋 Shreyans here, maker of MakersClaw.

We first launched MakersClaw here in June as AI employees you could hire into Slack, Teams and Telegram.

Today we're relaunching as part of Astra Day, after rebuilding the product around a different idea.


MakersClaw is no longer primarily a chatbot you give a role to. You give it a goal.


MakersClaw figures out what needs to exist to pursue that goal — an app, an agent, automations, or some combination of them — builds those things into your workspace, connects them to your tools and runs the work.


Sometimes that means a research agent. Sometimes it needs a lead inbox, CRM, approval queue or recurring workflow. Instead of forcing every job through chat, MakersClaw can build the interface appropriate for the work.


Why we rebuilt it

AI made building software dramatically cheaper. A founder can ship a product in a weekend. But selling it is still weekly, repetitive, tool-heavy work.


We thought agents should be able to do much more of that work.


The problem with the agents we were using was that they were still session-based. They'd complete a task, lose context, ask to be restarted and wait for another prompt.


MakersClaw 2.0 is built around work that continues.


Tell it something like:


"Help me find and reach our first 50 customers."


You can watch the first run, inspect what it built, approve the important decisions and set a budget. After that, it can keep running and come back when it needs you.


Company files, decisions and results live in shared workspace memory, so agents can pick up where previous work left off rather than starting from scratch.


Today we're starting with go-to-market: research, content, outbound, follow-ups and the surrounding workflows. The App Store is still small and there are integrations we haven't tested deeply yet.


That's part of why we're launching now.


Try giving MakersClaw one real growth job you need done this week. If it gets stuck, builds the wrong thing or asks you to do something it should have handled itself, tell me here.


I'll be around all day.

Guys, what an intense day, isn't it?

How mny new users did you manage to bring to your product today, and how much feedback did you get?

The idea of giving an agent a goal instead of just a task is really interesting. The part about it continuously running and building the workflows it needs around that goal is especially compelling.

Curious to see how this evolves as more real-world workflows get added. 🚀

items.title: Lumiko
items.name: Lumiko
items.summary: Screen recordings that edit themselves with Auto Zoom-Pan
items.description: Lumiko records your screen and edits the footage while you work. It tracks your cursor and clicks, then builds smooth zoom and pan moves over them automatically, no keyframes. Trim, split, and reorder clips on a timeline right in the browser. Smart Blur hides API keys and passwords in one drag. Add a webcam bubble, custom backgrounds, click effects. Exports up to 4K. Runs locally, no account, no upload queue. Free to start.
top_comments: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I built Lumiko because I kept losing an hour to keyframes after every five-minute recording. The zoom-and-pan you see in slick tutorial videos usually comes from someone manually placing markers over every click, and I got tired of it. Lumiko watches where your cursor goes while you record, then generates that zoom and pan movement on its own once you stop. You still get a full timeline editor for trimming and reordering clips, plus Smart Blur for hiding sensitive info like API keys before you share anything. Everything renders on your machine. No account, no upload step, no waiting on a server queue. Pro is $9, one time, no subscription. It removes the watermark, unlocks 4K exports, and covers 3 devices for life. Would love to hear what part of your current recording workflow eats the most time. That's what I'm building toward next.

Hey man, great UI. I tried it, some clicks are not registering (I am aware of merging zooms if they are too close) but some clicks are not registering on browser, and if I am recording the whole screen, on any app outside my browser when i click, there are no zoom events on timeline.
Am i missing some setting?

Also even that I have pinned the extension it still opens the full page.

Other than that its great experience. All the best with taking this forward 🙌

top_comments: This seems useful in heavy subagent tasks. Whats the comparative token usage lets say for claude code multi agents and using Toone??

Congrats on your launch @matheus_paranhos1 . The website looks great and the concept looks promising.

I really like the idea of repeatable workflows created once and the visualizing it as a graph is just chef's kiss as it makes things easy to understand for non tech people.

A few thoughts I had:

  1. I like the concept of the AI babysitting the workflow but the video also mentioned watching each task as it gets completed. The thing I like about Claude's agentic workflows is that I don't need to watch it work, I can just specify what I need to get done and how I like it to work so it only interrupts me when it is stuck or when I need to review so I'd probably not like to babysit and watch my own workflow in action. Kind of like a CI pipeline, I want to see where things broke as my tasks might take time to finish. Perhaps you meant it only the first time in the video so ignore if that is the case.

  2. I kind of do some similar things using Claude's md files and I ask it to visualize the workflow in a mermaid diagram. It doesn't look as cool as your UI but it does get the job done, what would you say are some other benefits beyond the UX? I do see the UX as a big benefit for non tech users.

  3. Do we have control about which model your tool will use once I give it access to my Anthropic key? This task probably doesn't need a sophisticated model for deep reasoning as this could have a cost implication.

  4. From a UX perspective:

    1. One thing I'd like is the ability to drag and drop nodes to edit the workflow than chatting again as I feel AI agents sometimes rework everything while dragging and dropping could take me seconds

    2. Adding a voice feature would be great as well not only from an ease of use perspective but imagine for use cases like accessibility and IOT integrations.

I hope this was helpful. Great idea, amazing execution on the website and I'm looking forward to playing with it when it goes live.

Well done and all the best.

Good luck with the launch, guys!

idea_items.title: 简历优化助手
idea_items.need_line: 求职者想用 AI 优化简历措辞，又怕通用 AI 擅自夸大或编造经历，导致面试追问和背调风险。
idea_items.status_line: 现在多是手动修改或用通用 AI 润色，但后者可能把“用过 Python”改成“精通 Python”，于是出现开源工具逐句比对原文、附改动说明和面试追问点，也有讨论提醒经历合并、学历拔高等造假风险。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的是“受控改写+可核验说明”方向：把每处改动的依据与原文对照、面试追问预测做成可交付说明文件，并支持按具体岗位 JD 做匹配改写，而不是无条件放大措辞。

idea_items.title: 邮件自动化工具
idea_items.need_line: 销售跟进中，用户需要按不同场景及时发出正确邮件并保证送达，避免依赖人工维护模板与节奏造成漏跟。
idea_items.status_line: 现在主要靠人工把跟进拆成12类邮件模板和节奏表执行，发送前再用邮箱有效性、邮箱与IP拉黑及投诉次数检测来保送达。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的是把客户沉默时长、报价有效期、节日与价格变动变成可触发的发送条件，并把每轮往来按客户沉淀为可检索线程，让跟进节奏由状态驱动。

idea_items.title: AI 财务管家
idea_items.need_line: 想快速弄清钱花在哪、毛利率为何下滑，但账目数据散落在凭证、报销、BI 等多个系统里，难以一处看清。
idea_items.status_line: 大家主要按功能拼凑现成工具：智能凭证与一键结转 SaaS、扫描流水查异常交易、BI 拖拽做看板，再用通用大模型对话追问，跨系统取数仍靠人工反复导表。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得继续跟踪两条产品化路径：一是把记账动作压缩到手机快捷指令级别、数据留在本地的个人现金流账本；二是对账、重复报销识别这类结果能被账目直接验证的窄任务自动化。

interest_sections.title: 简历优化助手
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，核心观察是简历优化的真实命题不是润色得更好看，而是在不虚构经历的前提下让HR快速抓到重点、并让候选人扛得住面试追问。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状是自己手改或用AI工具润色，但通用AI会替你编（写“用过Python”被改成“精通Python”），于是出现开源工具把改后结果逐句与原文比对、附改动说明和面试官可能追问的点，另一条讨论则集中在经历合并、学历拔高等造假做法的风险上。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是“受控改写+可核验说明”这类方向：把每处改动的依据与原文对照、以及面试追问预测做成可交付的说明文件，并支持按具体岗位JD做匹配改写，而不是无条件放大措辞。
